rules.statement: Pass a password across an asynchronous API as `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>`, encoded with `SecureEncoding.UTF8` into a caller-owned buffer rented from the pinned, zeroing `SecureMemoryPool<byte>`. Never pass it as a managed `string`.
rules.why: A managed string leaves the raw password on the GC heap. A pinned, zeroing buffer gets wiped, and a span can't cross an async boundary.
rules.check: Look for password or secret parameters typed `string` on store or credential methods, and for callers that build the bytes with `Encoding.UTF8` or a non-secure array instead of `SecureEncoding.UTF8` into `SecureMemoryPool<byte>`.

rules.statement: Make a credential store contract expose hashing and verification as first-class operations, such as add or set a password and verify a credential. Never expose a raw password-hash field or property.
rules.why: Exposing the hash leaks hashing semantics onto the public contract and forces every backend to reimplement it. The store should hash, compare and upgrade the hash itself.
rules.check: Look for store interfaces or public account models that have a `PasswordHash` (or similar) member, or that expect callers to hash or compare passwords themselves.

rules.statement: Have a store rotate the account's security stamp on every credential change, such as setting a password or adding an account with a password, and keep the stamp read-only to callers.
rules.why: The security stamp is a store-managed value that each credential change rotates. This is the pattern borrowed from ASP.NET Core Identity.
rules.check: Look for password-setting store code that doesn't regenerate the security stamp, or for a stamp with a public setter on the account contract.

rules.statement: Implement default password hashing as PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 through `Rfc2898DeriveBytes.Pbkdf2`, with versioned parameters and a rehash when a successful verification finds an outdated hash.
rules.why: Versioned parameters with rehash-on-verify let stored hashes be upgraded over time without forcing password resets.
rules.check: Look for hashers that use a different primitive, store unversioned parameters, or never upgrade the hash after a successful verify.

rules.statement: Make a DI extension method for a capability that needs a backing store take the store registration's marker builder, such as `IServiceBuilder<TLibrary>`, as a required parameter, and make every store registration (custom stores included) return that marker.
rules.why: A capability registered without a store then fails to compile, instead of failing at runtime.
rules.check: Look for capability registration methods that don't require the store's marker builder, and for store registrations that return a plain `IServiceCollection` or builder instead of the marker.

rules.statement: When more than one registration method can add the same strategy handler, register it with `TryAddEnumerable` so it ends up registered only once.
rules.why: Several capability registrations add the same enricher and subject validator, and each one must still run only once.
rules.check: Look for `AddSingleton`, `AddScoped` or `AddTransient` of a collection-style handler inside registration methods that hosts may call together.

rules.statement: Decide whether an optional protocol feature is supported by whether its capability handler is registered (a default handler answers 'unsupported' until an opt-in package replaces it), not by a configuration flag.
rules.why: This lets the core avoid depending on the capability's package, and only hosts that opt in pay for the feature's stack.
rules.check: Look for boolean options such as `EnablePasswordGrant` that gate a grant or feature, or for core packages that reference the capability's package directly.

rules.statement: In an OAuth token endpoint, answer a password-grant request with a rejected credential with `invalid_grant`. Use `unsupported_grant_type` only when no handler for the grant is registered.
rules.why: A rejected credential is an authentication failure, not a missing capability.
rules.check: Look for password-grant handlers that return `unsupported_grant_type` for a bad user name or password, or `invalid_grant` when the grant isn't configured at all.

rules.statement: Model a local account as an identity link whose issuer is this server (a self-issued issuer) and whose subject is the account id, with credential, profile and status data in a 1:1 companion record. Don't add password or profile columns to the identity link or to the principal.
rules.why: Keeping one link concept and one resolution path for local and external connections avoids always-null columns on external identities and prevents one human from being counted twice.
rules.check: Look for credential or profile fields added to principal or federated-identity entities, or for a second resolution path that maps accounts straight to principals.

rules.statement: Keep persisted payloads as concrete data-contract records and express pluggability through a store interface. Don't turn the record into an interface.
rules.why: Pluggability belongs to the store seam, and the payload should stay a plain data contract like every other.
rules.check: Look for interfaces introduced over persisted model records, such as an `IAccount` that a store's own type implements.

rules.statement: In an abstractions package, keep public signatures on BCL types such as `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>`. Take `NCode.Buffers` or other implementation dependencies only in implementation packages.
rules.why: This keeps the abstraction free of implementation dependencies, so other backends can implement it without taking those dependencies.
rules.check: Look for new `NCode.Buffers` (or similar) package references, or buffer types from those packages, in `*.Abstractions` projects' public APIs.
